# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support or product-feasibility decisions, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |

| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Preserve item identity through layout changes

Read [the collection guide](../../references/collections.md). The workflow is application advice, with documented support qualified by platform.

Inspect actual items, screen/code, target input/platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Determine whether visual recognition or text comparison drives selection; record selection, reorder, insertion, and scrolling behavior only when evidenced. Text-heavy comparison may belong in a list/table rather than a collection.

Choose a familiar row/grid before a custom arrangement. Size cells around meaningful imagery and labels, allowing focus/hover expansion without collision. Retain standard selection/editing interactions and use custom gestures only for a demonstrated task need. For iOS/iPadOS layout changes during manipulation, favor explicit triggers and preserve the person's location and selected item; do not reshuffle a live grid merely because a data property changed. The guide marks collections unsupported on watchOS, so adapt to a suitable list rather than assert parity.

Implement a requested collection or produce a cell/layout/interaction specification; review findings must name affected items or transitions. Specify stable identity and understandable insertion/deletion/reorder feedback as application decisions consistent with the guide.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a wallpaper grid reorders by popularity while someone drags an image, causing the target to move. Decision: dynamic ranking conflicts with manipulation. After: preserve the displayed order during the drag and expose an explicit refresh/sort action; animate a deliberate reorder while retaining selection.

Deliver the artifact and layout-change policy. Verify long labels, odd item counts, focused edge cells, reorder, and deletion of the selected item. Fail for overlapping focused cells, accidental activation during scrolling, or identity/location lost after a layout change. Report native focus/gesture execution separately from inspected logic.

Use [lists-and-tables](../apple-hig-lists-and-tables/SKILL.md) for text comparison, [image-views](../../../apple-hig-content/.topics/apple-hig-image-views/SKILL.md) for fitting, or [drag-and-drop](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-drag-and-drop/SKILL.md) for transfer behavior.

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Collections Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/collections) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A collection presents ordered content in a flexible visual layout, particularly well suited to imagery. ## Best practices Prefer the familiar horizontal row or grid before inventing a layout. Text-heavy content usually scans more efficiently in a table or list. Make items easy to reach and choose, leaving enough space around images for focus and hover effects to remain visible without overlap. Preserve standard selection, editing, and scrolling interactions; add custom gestures only where the task needs them. Standard insertion, deletion, and reorder animations can explain changes, with custom animation available when appropriate. ## Platform considerations No additional macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. Collections are unsupported in watchOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Treat dynamic layout changes cautiously. # Preserve relationships while available space changes

Read [Layout](../../references/layout.md). Inspect content priority, navigation, controls, supported environments, constraints, and current implementation. Identify design/review/adaptation mode and keep the existing layout system. Record actual available space and text/localization conditions; device names alone are insufficient evidence for a breakpoint.

Start with relationships: align peers, group related items, indent subordinates, and reveal secondary choices progressively. Place important content toward the leading/top region in the locale's reading order. Separate backgrounds that can extend beneath bars from important content/actions that must respect safe regions.

Choose adaptations from available width/height and environmental values, not a phone/tablet or portrait/landscape guess. Preserve selection, content, functionality, and idiom when columns collapse, actions overflow, or horizontal rows stack for larger text. Test the smallest and largest useful layouts first, then intermediate resizing, longer localization, direction changes, and display accommodations. Crop decorative backgrounds without distorting aspect ratio or hiding essential imagery.

Apply platform conditions deliberately: Mac essential controls cannot depend on a bottom edge that may be offscreen; TV content needs the guide's overscan insets and focus-expansion room; Watch normally needs very few side-by-side actions. visionOS windows/volumes should resize, use meaningful bounds, and avoid inline 3D crowding controls; use separate volumes for model-centric work. Read numeric platform specifications from the guide rather than generalizing one platform's spacing.

**Before → decision → after:** A reading list positions Delete at a fixed bottom coordinate and fixes each row to one line. Decision: resized windows and enlarged titles need flow-based layout. After, row height/wrapping adapt, secondary actions remain reachable through contextual overflow, and the selected article persists when the sidebar collapses.

Deliver corrected layouts/constraints or implementation plus an environment matrix. Fail if a required action disappears, related items detach, content overlaps hardware/bars, or resizing changes the task's meaning. Report tested dimensions/settings; static or Linux checks cannot establish native safe-area/focus behavior absent supported execution.

Use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for text behavior, [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for direction, and [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for 3D position/scale.

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Layout Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. # Preserve readable hierarchy as text grows

Read [Typography](../../references/typography.md). Inspect the actual text roles, font files/styles, platform, viewing context, and resizing behavior. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Use the guide's platform style/size tables when exact values matter; do not reproduce the entire specification or confuse its minimum with a comfortable default.

Assign semantic roles before choosing sizes: title, body, supporting detail, and actionable label need a clear relationship. Prefer system text styles and runtime font APIs so optical design/tracking adapt to size. If a custom face is needed, verify weight/legibility and provide equivalent text-size and Bold Text behavior; thin faces may need more size than the table suggests. Use loose leading for sustained/wide reading, avoiding tight leading across three or more lines.

Decide how content expands. Grow containers, permit labels to wrap, stack timestamps/glyphs, and reduce columns rather than aggressively truncating essential reading. Scale meaningful glyphs with the text. Preserve hierarchy while prioritizing the content people intend to read; not every decorative/transient number must grow identically.

Apply platform differences: macOS has no Dynamic Type, so use appropriate standard-control fonts and explicit product text accommodations rather than promising that API behavior. On visionOS, favor readable 2D text, explicit styles for New York, little extrusion, and viewer-facing object labels; do not rely on cast shadows against unpredictable surroundings. Watch uses its own font conventions, including complication typography.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a book list fixes custom thin titles to one line and leaves status glyphs tiny at larger text sizes. Decision: reading and status must remain usable together. After, titles use a legible role/weight, wrap into growing rows, supporting text stacks, and meaningful glyphs scale while selection/actions stay available.

Deliver corrected type roles, resizing rules, or implementation with supported-size examples. Fail if essential content is clipped without a full-text route, hierarchy collapses, or Bold Text/custom sizing breaks controls. Record tested sizes and actual font measurements; device-distance legibility, native shaping, and spatial comfort need supported execution.

Use [Layout](../apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for reflow, [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for task-level access, or [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for mixed-script alignment.

# Separate image presentation from action

Read [the image-view guide](../../references/image-views.md). Use the following as application advice, preserving the requested stack.

Inspect the image assets and container, target platform, intended focal content, and whether the request is to create, review, or adapt. Determine whether the image is decorative, informative, editable, or an action. Record intrinsic resolution/aspect ratio, crop/fit behavior, overlays, and animation source when available; a screenshot cannot establish frame preparation or input semantics.

Choose fitting from the content's purpose: preserve the whole image when cropping loses information; allow deliberate cropping when the focal subject survives. Do not stretch photographs to satisfy a container. If activation performs an action, use button semantics rather than attaching an unexplained gesture to a display image. On Mac, choose an image well for copy/paste/drag/Delete editing. Prefer symbols or template imagery for interface glyphs rather than embedding their appearance as arbitrary pictures.

Apply the choice in code or supply an annotated container/asset specification; reviews must identify a crop, semantic, or legibility defect with a concrete repair. For text overlays, inspect both bright and dark image regions and provide supporting treatment where needed. Prepare animation frames consistently rather than depending on repeated runtime rescaling. For tvOS retain intended layered transparency; for visionOS choose a window image, spatial presentation, or scene mechanism deliberately instead of flattening every image. The guide mentions implementation capabilities, not proof that a supplied framework supports them.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a museum map stretches into a portrait card, with a “View route” gesture on the picture. Decision: distortion damages map meaning and the action lacks button behavior. After: fit the complete map within the card and provide a named `View Route` image/button action; decorative framing remains outside its accessible name.

Deliver the changed asset/container behavior and semantic purpose. Verify key content survives aspect changes, overlays remain readable, and actionable imagery works through keyboard/assistive activation. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. # Operate on buttons

Read [the buttons guide](../../references/buttons.md) before making HIG claims. This procedure is application advice for turning that guide into an artifact; platform facts and dimensions come from the guide. Preserve the user's framework and authorized scope.

## Establish the action contract

Inspect the supplied screen, code, prototype, or brief. Identify the target platform, input methods, surrounding task, and requested mode: create, review, or adapt. For each consequential button, record its visible label or symbol, activation outcome, affected object, reversibility, current role/default status, and actual hit region if available. A screenshot can establish visible styling; it cannot establish hit geometry, keyboard behavior, or accessible names. Mark those as unknown and inspect implementation when available.

Classify the action before styling it. An immediate command fits a button. A persistent on/off setting may need a toggle; choosing one of several persistent options may need a segmented control or picker; a menu-opening control needs the corresponding menu button behavior. Retain a button when its action is to open that choice, but distinguish opening from committing a choice.

## Make and apply the consequential choices

1. Write an outcome-specific short verb phrase, or use a familiar symbol whose meaning survives its context. Give an icon-only control an accessible name that states the action. Do not assume a tooltip replaces the name. On Mac, an ellipsis indicates that another window, view, or app requires further input; add it based on the continuation, not merely because an operation takes time.
2. Assign semantic roles from consequences. Prefer one or two prominent likely actions per view and use style rather than unequal sizes to rank related choices. A primary/default action should normally be the likely nondestructive choice. If destruction is involved, consult the alerts topic before deciding confirmation and Return behavior: the guide explicitly allows a deliberate-destruction alert exception, so “destructive can never be default” is not a universal rule. Cancel abandons the current task; it is not a generic label for completing it.
3. Choose the system control/style when available, retaining its states and accessibility behavior. For a custom control, specify perceivable press feedback and preserve meaningful focus, enabled/disabled, and selected states as applicable. State the reason for a disabled action when the surrounding context does not explain it. This is application advice, not a new Apple requirement to add all states to every button.
4. Check visual and selectable geometry separately. Apply the guide's target and separation rules for the actual platform; a small glyph or small visual style does not establish a small hit region. On visionOS, retain a discernible shape/fill, use standard audible/state feedback, and inspect center spacing and hover overlap. Do not propose unsupported custom hover effects or haptics there. On watchOS, choose inline versus toolbar placement deliberately; preserve common heights for peer controls and use short labels for side-by-side actions. On Mac, distinguish view-body square/image/help buttons from toolbar items; apply the help-button placement/count rules only when designing Help.
5. Only when the command has delayed completion, define the initiating, waiting, and resolved behavior. On iOS/iPadOS, use the activating button's activity indication as described in the guide, preserving context and replacing its image when appropriate. Specify how duplicate activation is handled and what success or failure means in the product; do not promise network completion from a press animation.

Perform the authorized work: implement the controls in the supplied project for a build request; produce an annotated control specification for a design request; or report evidence-backed defects and exact corrections for a review. For adaptation, map each affected control to its destination platform rather than copying appearance alone.

## Deliver and verify

Return the changed artifact or a compact button contract containing label/name, outcome, role/default, style/placement, target region, and relevant state behavior. In review mode attach findings to identifiable controls and separate observed defects from checks requiring execution.

Verify that activation reaches the named outcome; cancellation leaves the intended prior state; keyboard/default activation cannot commit an unintended outcome; focus and accessible names identify the action; and enlarged labels do not clip or overlap adjacent targets. Measure hit regions from layout/runtime data when available. Fail the design if a destructive consequence is mislabeled, peer targets overlap, an icon has no discoverable name, or custom press feedback is absent. State separately which checks were inspected in source, exercised, or remain Apple-device checks; Linux inspection does not prove gaze, VoiceOver, haptics, or native rendering.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** A Mac photo organizer has equally prominent `Go`, `Remove`, and `Close` buttons. `Go` opens export settings; `Remove` deletes a selection with undo; `Close` finishes editing metadata.

**Decision:** The labels hide three different contracts. Export requires further input; routine reversible removal does not by itself justify a confirmation alert; finishing edits should name completion. The export task, rather than removal, is the likely action on this screen.

**After:** Specify `Export…` as the prominent action opening export settings, `Remove Photos` as a lower-emphasis command with a visible Undo path, and `Done` for finishing metadata edits. Inspect actual save semantics before changing `Close` to `Done`. Verify the Return mapping, undo restoration, and that each accessible name matches the resulting action. These product choices are an example application, not facts about the unseen implementation.

## Conditional handoffs

Load alerts for consequential confirmation/default decisions; toggles or segmented-controls for persistent selection; pop-up-buttons or pull-down-buttons for menu-opening behavior; toolbars when placement belongs to window chrome; and accessibility when naming, focus, contrast, or target access needs deeper work. Keep this button contract as the input to the next topic.

# Buttons Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Style](#Style) - [Content](#Content) - [Role](#Role) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) A button performs an immediate action. Its visual style, visible symbol/text, and semantic role work together to explain what activation does. ## Best practices Allow enough surrounding space for clear separation and easy selection. General hit regions should be at least 44×44 pt; visionOS targets need 60×60 pt. Custom buttons always need press feedback. ## Style Prefer system styles for built-in states, accessibility, and appearance adaptation. Use one or two prominent buttons per view for likely actions. Distinguish a preferred option through style rather than making related buttons different sizes. Keep label colors distinct from colorful content; the default monochrome often works best over rich backgrounds. ## Content Use a familiar symbol for a familiar action; use a short title-case verb phrase when words are clearer. Mac and visionOS can provide brief hover tooltips; text-labeled buttons usually explain themselves. ## Role Normal has no special meaning; primary is the expected/default action; Cancel abandons the current action; destructive signals data loss. Roles affect rendering, such as accent fill for primary and red for destructive. Primary can respond to Return and close a temporary view. # Adaptive photo collection specification

Platform: iOS/iPadOS, iPhone and iPad, including rotation and resizable iPad windows. Task: browse an album, identify a photo, open its full image, and select multiple photos. No framework is prescribed by the supplied brief. The rules below replace fixed six-column layout, rotation-cleared selection, thumbnail-only meaning, and blank empty albums.

## Layout and cell contract

Use a familiar vertically scrolling collection in stable album order. Default order is capture date descending, with stable photo ID as tie-breaker; missing dates follow dated items. Keep existing order until a deliberate reload after external changes; never reorder while scrolling, selecting, or resizing. Item count does not change density or interaction.

Let W be safe-area content width after 16 pt leading/trailing margins. Use 8 pt gaps. At ordinary Dynamic Type sizes, columns C = max(1, floor((W + 8) / 112)); image side S = (W - 8 × (C - 1)) / C. Thus 104 pt is the target minimum image width, an app choice, not an Apple minimum. At accessibility text sizes use one column with a 104 pt thumbnail and a wrapping text region alongside it; stack thumbnail above text when W < 260 pt. Grow row height to fit all text. No horizontal scrolling. Short windows retain vertical scrolling and reachable controls.

Examples (all widths in points, after device safe-area exclusion but before margins):

| Available width | W | Columns | Image side |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 320 | 288 | 2 | 140 |
| 390 | 358 | 3 | 114 |
| 768 | 736 | 6 | 116 |
| 1024 | 992 | 8 | 117 |

Do not force six columns on narrow iPad windows or phones. The same available width produces the same grid rules on both devices. Respect system safe regions for all content and actions. Recompute on resize, orientation, text-size, or Display Zoom changes; these environmental changes may reflow immediately, but must preserve identity and location.

Each cell contains an undistorted square thumbnail, then a wrapping caption on a solid system background: supplied photo title (fallback filename), and localized capture date (fallback “Date unknown”). Use system body style for title, secondary text style for date, supporting Dynamic Type and Bold Text. No essential caption truncation. Deliberate aspect-fill cropping is a browse preview only; detail presents the entire image with aspect-fit, including panoramas and document edges. A neutral unavailable-image placeholder keeps the same geometry and text.

Provide meaningful existing photo descriptions as text alternatives. If none exists, announce title/filename and date and explicitly use “No description available”; do not infer a subject or imply metadata describes the image. Detail exposes any supplied description in readable text too. This makes identification available without thumbnail recognition, while acknowledging absent descriptions limit access to visual content.

## Interaction and state

Use system collection selection and named button activation rather than gesture-only image actions. In browse mode activating a cell opens detail by stable ID; its accessible name combines title, date and description if available, with a button role. Detail includes a labeled Back action returning to the originating cell and scroll position.

A visible “Select” button enters selection mode. Cell activation then toggles selection; expose selected state programmatically and with a checkmark plus outline, independent of color. Show “N selected” and “Done”; Done exits selection mode and clears selection deliberately. Select is unavailable for a genuinely empty album. All controls have at least 44 × 44 pt activation regions, separated without overlapping adjacent targets. Standard pressed, disabled, focus and pointer feedback remain visible within cell bounds. New external items are held behind a visible “Show updates” button; activation applies the new snapshot while retaining surviving IDs and anchor. Enlarged text, focus and hover must not overlap neighbors or hide actions. Use semantic system colors; check light/dark and Increase Contrast against actual rendered backgrounds. Required state information never relies on color alone.

Use the same collection for 20 and 20,000 items. Virtualize/reuse cells; load ordered metadata in pages of 200, with total count and an indexed stable-ID lookup so anchor restoration can fetch the relevant page directly. Keep at most five metadata pages resident; retain selected IDs separately. Preserve a stable order snapshot across page boundaries with no duplicates or omissions. Do not require decoding earlier photos to reach a later page.

Cancel obsolete requests on reuse and bind completion to both stable ID and request generation so a late image cannot populate another cell. Use a bounded decoded-thumbnail cache (initial budget 64 MiB) and at most four simultaneous decodes; release offscreen decoded images under memory pressure. Full-resolution decoding occurs only for detail and is released when no longer needed. These are initial engineering budgets requiring profiling, not HIG performance guarantees. For 20 items this path can complete in one page; for 20,000 it must never eagerly decode all originals or instantiate all cells.

Initial metadata pending: show “Loading photos” until the first page resolves; never claim the album is empty before success. With known items, preserve the grid while further pages load and show a trailing “Loading more photos” status. Thumbnail loading/failure keeps cell text and selection usable. Initial failure: “Photos couldn’t be loaded” with “Retry”. Later-page failure retains existing cells and adds “More photos couldn’t be loaded” with Retry for that page; prevent duplicate retries while pending. Errors do not clear state or alter order.
